iterations.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. One implementable Minecraft multiblock smithy design, a fresh redesign of the leftmost brick workstation in the attached screenshot. Reference image is for Minecraft scale, actual red brick and wood texture language ONLY; do not preserve its crude existing shape and do not depict the other machines. Show a single isolated finished smithy on a small stone workshop floor, three-quarter front view, eye height slightly elevated, plain muted background, entire silhouette clearly visible. Faithful 32x-like Minecraft pixel textures, crisp block geometry, restrained realistic shader lighting, no photoreal miniature or painterly shapes. Tesla-era practical industrial artisan workshop, handsome and sturdy, not fantasy medieval clutter. Rough envelope four full blocks wide, three deep, four high. Left half: coal forge of red brick, waist-high open hearth with glowing coals, dark iron hearth liner, a generously accessible rectangular opening, masonry rear and side support carrying a stepped brick smoke hood and one narrow square chimney. Hood shoulders are clear HALF-BLOCK STAIRSTEPS, not diagonal smooth slopes; no unsupported floating lintel. Right half: low substantial dark timber workbench with half-block-thick slab top, half-by-half-block quarter-beam legs and stretchers, clear empty space beneath. A recognizable Minecraft anvil on the bench and a modest small iron vise at its outer end. Brick cheek between fire and timber. At front under hearth, one inset iron ash-door/controller face with understated brass latch, accessible from front. Mostly brick and timber, dark iron on working surfaces; no copper slab, no railings, no decorative gears, no machinery added beyond a forge and bench. Deliberately show our saw-cut construction: slabs 1x1x0.5, quarter BEAMS 1x0.5x0.5, smallest cubes 0.5x0.5x0.5. These shape hearth lip, hood shoulders, bench top, open bench supports and two small corbels, all aligned to the HALF-BLOCK grid. Only anvil, vise and controller hardware use smaller custom-model pixels. Do not model masonry as lots of separate tiny bricks, textures depict brick mortar. Timber legs sit firmly on ground; masonry firmly supported. Attractive readable silhouette with tall forge on left and low bench on right. Warm localized ember light without darkening the rest. No text, dimensions, labels, UI, people, loose floating objects, multiple views or competing concepts. Keep enough front and right side visible to understand how to build it.
iterations.review: Revise: strong forge/bench silhouette and supported masonry; bench has unnecessary fine cuffs and anvil resembles an I pedestal.

iterations.prompt: Edit this smithy concept, preserving its composition, warm red-brick forge, open hearth, supported stepped hood, chimney, side bench, vise, controller door, lighting and Minecraft texture style. Two precise corrections only: (1) replace the blunt I-shaped metal pedestal on the bench with a recognizable Minecraft blacksmith anvil, with an elongated flat striking face and a clearly projecting stepped horn on its left end, compact waist and flared foot, made from simple Minecraft cuboids; (2) simplify the wood bench supports to uniform square HALF-BLOCK-thick posts and one plain matching crossbeam, without tiny decorative cuffs, collars, narrow strips or feet. Bench top is a plain half-block slab with wood texture, no thin apron lip. Bench underside stays open. Structural cut-block geometry is only full cubes, 1x1x0.5 slabs, 1x0.5x0.5 beams and 0.5-cubed eighths; smaller pixels belong only to anvil/vice/controller custom-model hardware. Keep the attractive high forge/low bench silhouette, no extra props or labels. One polished implementable Minecraft mockup.
iterations.review: Selected concept: clearer anvil horn and plain open timber supports. Supported hearth, brick/timber separation, front access and coherent material family. Illustration is not an exact block blueprint: native blockout must quantize shoulders, lip, bench and feet to half-grid and validate overall dimensions. Anvil/vice/controller are small-model fittings, not arbitrarily thin saw parts. No new functionality implied.
